videos.title: 美光暴涨！AI能够改变“周期”规律吗？ | Micron | MU | 镁光 | 半导体 | HBM | 高带宽内存 |  三星 |  海力士
videos.transcript: Micron released an earnings report so  incredible it’s hard to believe: Q1  revenue hit $ 5.42 billion, with $  13.32 billion for the full year—more  than triple the previous year's $ 3.74  billion—and the company expects to  set new records next quarter. It sounds  like a high-growth tech company, but  historically, Micron has always been  considered a cyclical stock. So the  question is: has AI truly made the  cycle obsolete? Or have we once again  fallen for the most expensive phrase in  investing? "This time is different." In  this video, I want to use Micron's  earnings report to talk about what I  believe is the most important and  unavoidable topic in investing: the  cycle. Hi everyone, this is US Stock  Doctor, sharing insights on US stocks  every week. For today's video, make  sure to watch until the end. In the  first part of the video, let's discuss  why Micron is performing so strongly  this round. If you are already very  familiar with what Micron does, feel  free to skip to this timestamp. Micron  mainly produces memory: the chips  responsible for storing data in  computers, smartphones, and servers.  This is mainly divided into two  categories: DRAM, which is memory used  for temporary data during operations,  and NAND, which is flash storage used  for files in phones and hard drives.  Historically, the two types of products  produced by memory manufacturers have  had two distinct characteristics. First , commoditization. For example, when we  buy a laptop, we only look at the  capacity of the memory and hard drive.  As for who manufactures them, the vast  majority of people couldn't care less.  Because these products are essentially  standardized, they are interchangeable  between manufacturers, meaning there is  severe commoditization. When products  are severely commoditized, it is  difficult to rely on brand pricing.  Second is the marginal effect. Since  the costs of factory equipment and  production lines are mostly fixed, the  marginal cost of producing memory  sticks is relatively low. This is a bit  like oil companies, where equipment  costs are high, but once the process is  running, production scales easily.  Producing less just means earning less,  while producing more means earning more ; as long as memory prices rise  slightly, the extra revenue almost  entirely becomes profit. Due to the  commoditization of products and low  marginal costs, the storage industry  has been trapped in a profit cycle for  decades. Prices mainly depend on supply  and demand: when demand is strong,  prices rise, leading manufacturers to  expand capacity. As supply increases,  prices fall, profits shrink, and  manufacturers cut investment, causing  supply to contract. This eventually  weeds out poorly managed companies  before the next cycle begins. This  makes these companies money-printing  machines during upturns and meat  grinders during downturns, reflecting  highly distinct cyclical  characteristics. Therefore, the capital  market typically gives these highly  cyclical companies low valuations,  usually around 10 times. So, why do  these storage manufacturers seem to  have broken out of the cycle this time?  We all know the answer. That answer is  AI. AI has driven demand toward HBM and  high-performance memory. As prices have  risen and operating leverage has been  magnified, profits have exploded. Many  people might ask: since we all consider  these cyclical stocks that earn  cyclical profits, why does this stock  price surge make so many people feel  that this cycle is different from the  past? I have summarized the answer in  three points. First, industry  expectations show that the share of HBM  and server DRAM in AI servers is rising  rapidly, and the share of memory in AI  infrastructure spending is also  expanding. This is not just a simple  replacement cycle, but a continuous  infrastructure build-out. Second,  top-tier customers have locked in  capacity through strategic agreements  by paying prepayments or deposits.  Taking Micron as an example, the  proportion of such agreements extending  to 2030 and 2031 has increased  significantly, with a massive scale of  remaining performance obligations.  Third, while these companies mainly  produced highly commoditized memory and  hard drives in the past, the product  characteristics of AI-related offerings  have led to shifts in their business  models. First, the technical  architecture differences are  significant, increasing manufacturing  complexity and entry barriers. Second,  customer customization raises the entry  threshold, as these major customers all  sign long-term supply agreements. All  of these factors have weakened the  cyclical nature of these storage stocks . However, we still need to clearly  distinguish two things: AI requires  more HBM, a fact visible in financial  reports. How long this demand will last  and how large it will be depends not  only on the judgment of Micron's  management but also on market  expectations, which is to say, investor  sentiment. Micron emphasizes that AI is  driving the entire storage ecosystem of  HBM, DRAM, and SSDs. However, this is  the company's own assessment of the  industry; we can use it as a reference,  but we must never treat it as an  objective fact. So, regarding storage  stocks, is this truly a brand-new  growth story, or just another very  strong cyclical story? Next, we will  enter the second part: why is money in  cyclical stocks so hard to make? Former  Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan  once said, "We only know it's a bubble  when it bursts." Cycles have a similar  concept: the last day of a bull market  is the beginning of a bear market, and  the last day of a bear market happens  to be the start of a bull market. The  strangest thing about a cycle is that  it never tells you when the top is. On  the contrary, it presents a mountain of  data to show us how good things are  this time: great orders, great prices,  great profits, confident management,  and analysts constantly raising  expectations. For example, take a  cyclical stock: profit of 1 billion in  year one, 2 billion in year two, 4  billion in year three, and 8 billion in  year four. Seeing profits double  continuously, we start to feel that  this company's growth potential is  outstanding. But the real question is:  is this 8 billion the normal profit it  can earn in the future, or is it the  profit at the peak of the cycle? This  question is almost impossible to answer  objectively during an upturn, because  all signals reinforce the same judgment . We begin to believe that past  patterns might not apply this time, and  this is what Howard Marks repeatedly  warns us about: "This time is different ." As the co-founder of Oaktree Capital , his memos, updated periodically on  their website, are required reading  that Buffett has always recommended to  us ordinary investors. In his discourse  on cycles, he has emphasized more than  once that when a cycle begins or ends  is basically impossible to predict, but  we can strive to judge another fact:  roughly where we are in the cycle.  Predicting the future asks us to name  the "peak" date, while judging our  position involves looking at current  prices, sentiment, supply, and  investment behavior—whether people  are pessimistic or optimistic, whether  no one dares to expand production or  everyone is rushing to do so. To  clarify, Howard Marks is talking about  general cycles and human behavior, not  making a specific judgment on Micron,  right? It's not that anyone who says " this time is different" is necessarily  wrong. Sometimes it really is different , just like the internet or smartphones , which truly changed their industries.  But the real question is what exactly  is different: has the demand structure  changed, has the supply structure  shifted, has the competitive landscape  evolved, has the pace of capital  expenditure changed, or is it simply  that investors are more optimistic than  before? The former points are real  changes, while the last one is merely  sentiment. The danger lies in jumping  directly from "this time is truly  different" to "all past rules no longer  apply"—there is a vast gap between  those two statements. Returning to  Micron, the market has reason to  believe this time is different because  AI demand is clearly structural. HBM  has higher barriers, tighter  integration with advanced packaging and  GPUs, and AI customers prioritize  supply, willing to lock in capacity  with long-term contracts, while new  capacity takes longer to build. Each of  these factors could make the cycle  longer and stronger, but a longer cycle  and the disappearance of the cycle are  two different things. Since the cycle  hasn't disappeared, let's move on to  the third part: how should we actually  view AI's impact on the cycle? Let me  share my judgment first—note that  this is my analysis, not a proven fact.  AI may have changed the shape of the  cycle, but it certainly will not make  the cycle disappear. I think we should  focus not on how much money Micron is  making, but on what changes have  actually occurred in the industry's  supply and demand. As mentioned in the  first part, profit is just a result.  Regarding supply and demand, to  understand AI's impact on this memory  cycle, we need to look at three levels:  supply, demand, and pricing. The first  layer is demand, which determines how  far the cycle can go. In the past,  memory relied mainly on PCs and  smartphones, with limited market growth . Now, with AI data centers added,  we've moved from a mobile-driven cycle  to one that now includes AI  infrastructure. So we must look at two  things: first, AI capital expenditure —are major clients like Nvidia,  Amazon, Google, and Meta continuing to  increase their investment? If demand is  strong, but the support for that demand  appears to be slowing significantly, we  must re-evaluate. The second is whether  HBM demand itself remains strong, and  how the pricing, capacity, and customer  certification are holding up.  Especially with HBM4, the next  generation of technological upgrades  could either solidify barriers or  reshuffle the industry. Second is the  discussion of supply, which determines  when the cycle will turn. If demand  doubles and supply also doubles, prices  may not necessarily rise. The  characteristic of memory is that supply  is slow; you have to build plants, buy  equipment, adjust processes, improve  yields, and pass customer  certifications. Thus, demand shifts,  supply lags, leading to price hikes and  explosive profits. This is the current  situation. So, when will supply catch  up? It depends on two things. First is  capital expenditure, as today's capital  expenditure determines future supply.  Therefore, to judge if industry profits  are high, we can't just look at how  much a company earns; we must ask if  the industry is expanding capacity  frantically. If everyone believes  prices will remain high for years, they  will invest aggressively, which may set  the stage for the next phase. However,  it must be clear that increased capital  expenditure does not equal an immediate  bottom; it only indicates that future  supply is growing. Second is the  timeline for new capacity to come  online. We cannot just look at  investment announcements, but must see  when facilities are built, production  scales up, and effective supply is  truly formed. Announcements and actual  supply are two different things. Third  is price; price is the most honest  signal, telling us whether changes have  truly occurred. First, we need to  monitor: are the prices of DRAM and  NAND still rising? Has the pace of  growth slowed down? Is customer  inventory healthy? If inventory begins  to pile up, it indicates that supply is  starting to change. Second is long-term  agreements. Micron emphasizes that  strategic customer agreements provide  better future revenue visibility, which  is good, but improved visibility  doesn't mean the cycle has disappeared;  agreements lock in volume and price for  a period, not the industry-wide supply  and demand. Thus, demand determines how  far the cycle goes, supply determines  when the cycle shifts, and price  determines whether the change has truly  happened—these three are intertwined.  Seeing this, I believe many may feel  I've made things more confusing,  leaving you unsure whether to invest in  storage companies like Micron. I think  my purpose has been achieved, because  this video isn't meant to tell you if  you should buy Micron or not, but to  share where the real difficulty in  investing in these stocks lies. If you  don't have a deep understanding of the  demand, supply, and price factors I  mentioned, then your purchase of these  stocks is very likely blind, or will at  least significantly increase your  chance of losing money. If you aren't  absolutely certain, you might want to  do as I do and stay away from these  highly cyclical storage stocks. Of  course, I am not denying in this video  that AI has brought structural changes  in demand to the storage industry.  HBM's technical barriers are indeed  higher, supply improvements are more  difficult, and wealthy major clients  are willing to pay more to maintain  supply stability. These factors have  significantly extended this cycle, but  as long as there is supply, capital  expenditure, and price competition, the  cycle can never be completely  eliminated. It may become longer, more  complex, and fluctuate in ways  different from what we previously  understood, but the cycle itself still  exists. So when a company delivers its  most dazzling financial results in  history, we shouldn't just look at how  much higher it can go; we should focus  on whether its current profit is the  company's long-term capability or just  a gift from the cycle in the short term . The hardest part of investing has  never been understanding current  financial reports, but rather, once  financial reports are compounded by  industry cycles and macroeconomics, it  becomes difficult to judge the  company's true current state. I have  always believed that the most expensive  words in investing are "this time is  different." So, for Micron and even the  storage industry, is it truly " different this time," or have we once  again fallen for "this time is  different"? I welcome you all to share  your thoughts with me in the comments  section. Alright, that is the cycle I  wanted to discuss with everyone using  Micron's latest financial report as a  basis. Next, let's move on to the  portfolio disclosure. Hello, everyone.  The return for this week is 2.23%.  Since March 2022, the total account  return is 252.17%. There is only the  weekly $ 100 investment in Microsoft,  with no other changes. This week, I  want to talk about Eli Lilly. At the  recently concluded EASD 2024, Eli Lilly  announced the phase 2b data for its  latest multi-target combination weight  loss regimen. Let me first clarify what  this multi-target combination regimen  is: it is not a single triple-target  molecule, but rather Lilly combining  its existing dual-target weight loss  drug tirzepatide with a single-target  drug, orforglipron, to act on three  targets simultaneously. Lilly hopes to  push weight loss results even further  by layering different mechanisms. This  phase 2b trial enrolled 700 patients  who were obese or overweight and also  had type 2 diabetes, with a treatment  duration of 48 weeks, and the results  were indeed very impressive. In the  highest dose group, which was 9mg of  orforglipron plus the current highest  dose of 15mg of tirzepatide, the  average weight loss reached 23.3%. For  comparison, using 15mg of tirzepatide  alone for 48 weeks resulted in an  average weight loss of 14.8%. In other  words, in this experiment, adding  orforglipron increased weight loss by  8.5%. Regarding blood sugar, HbA1c in  the highest dose group decreased by 2.9 %, while tirzepatide alone decreased it  by 2.4%. However, there is a question  here that is very worth noting for  investors: if the effect is  significantly stronger, what is the  cost? The answer is gastrointestinal  side effects and the discontinuation  rate. The most common adverse reactions  in the trials remain gastrointestinal  issues such as nausea, diarrhea,  constipation, and vomiting, most of  which occur during the dose-escalation  phase. What is worth noting here is  that adverse events are more common in  the combination therapy group, with the  high-dose multi-target combination  group reporting an adverse event rate  as high as 27%, compared to only 2.9%in  the Retatrutide group. In other words,  the key issue with this drug is not  whether it can help lose more weight,  but whether it can help more patients  stick with the treatment, which is  precisely why Eli Lilly is the company  most worth watching right now. 同样是16次里有16次都出现了上涨，没有一次例外。所以以上这两套数据都告诉我们，在过去六十多年里，如果我们在中期选举年的秋天因为害怕而卖出了，那每一次都是错误的决定，因为你会完全踏空了之后的反弹，除非你非常精准的卖在了中期选举年中的最高点，又买在了当年的最低点，那当然这是一个非常难做到的事情。 不过为了完整性，我也要给朋友们分享事情的全貌，就是这16个样本不算特别多，因为从1960年以来，随便挑一个12个月的区间美股本来就有大约70%的概率是涨的。 所以中期选举年之后的这个规律，与其说是这个事件本身创造了一个上涨，不如说它放大了一个本来就存在的长期趋势。总而言之，以上九月份的规律以及中期选举年的规律都告诉我们。 在九月到十月份这个期间中大盘很有可能出现回调，这的确是一个大概率事件，但是回调的幅度很可能没有我们预期的那么大。更加重要的是，即便发生回调，反弹也会来的。 的非常迅速，而且幅度很有可能远远大于之前的回调。那讲完了历史规律，我们来看一下今年的情况，因为今年我们还面临一个特殊情况，就是9月15日到16日的美联储会议。 现在美联储的主席是沃什，上周五他在杰克逊霍尔的演讲里说，通胀的底层趋势没有实质性改善，所以美联储还有工作要做。然后因为这句话，市场就更加相信美联储会在九月份加息，而且在那之前，市场已经看到九月那次会议中是九比三的分裂投票，有三位委员公开反对按兵不动，主张直接加息。 所以他的这番话出来以后，市场迅速对九月份的加息重新定价，从原本大概率不加息的预期一路翻转，到了现在，将近70%的概率会在九月份加息。 那这件事对美股市场的冲击远远大于九月份的规律和中期选举。因为在过去两三年中，我们习惯的剧本是降息还是不降息，而现在突然变成了加不加息。 这是一个方向性的改变，而这个市场的估值，尤其是AI相关的高估值板块，是建立在利率往下走的假设上的。如果这个假设被推翻了，估值需要重新计算，这才是九月份真正的风险来源。 历史规律只是给它加了一层放大器。而且本周五还有一份八月份的非农就业数据，这份数据现在变成了双刃剑，数据太强，坐实加息数据太弱，市场又要担心经济衰退。 那上一份七月份的就业报告就已经显示美国出现了净减少的岗位。所以这个周五无论数字往哪边走，波动都不会。小尤其是如果出现了特别强劲的数据，那一定会给市场造成巨大的冲击。 我们一定要提前做好准备，但我们很有可能看到的是市场出现一个两极化的情况，那些当下盈利能力不足债务过高的公司，在加息的预期变动中会遭到很大的冲击。 一但对于那些当下基本面就非常强劲的。 公司，他们反而会吸引到很多热钱，从那些低质量的公司中又重新回到他们之中。所以我们还是要关心公司的本身。在刚刚结束的这个财报季中，AI基础设施这条链上的公司。 几乎全线超预期了，订单的能见度还在继续往后延。最能说明问题的一个数字就是前五大云厂商的资本开支，今年合计大约为八千亿美元，明年预期要涨到1.3万亿。 所以这不是一个正在减速的产业该有的曲线。因此，我们要思考这两条线的关系，一条线是利率，它决定我们愿意为未来的现金流付多少倍的估值。另一条线是这些公司实际现在就赚到的钱，他决定未来的现金流本身有多少。那现在的情况是，第一条线的确在恶化，但第二条线明显在加速，这就是我们反复讲的那个区别。 当股票出现下跌时，到底是估值的消化还是基本面的恶化？ 估值的消化，最典型的就是此前存储股所经历的大规模下跌。那这是好公司被便宜的卖掉，因为热钱暂时流走了，但基本面恶化是完全不同的情况，它是公司本身出了问题，前者是机会，后者是陷阱。所以相信很多朋友们现在手里有大量的AI股票，我们一定要区分手中的这些股票。 到底，他们现在是已经有了明显的基本面改善，还是依然处在一个炒概念的阶段？ 这将决定当这样的市场冲击来临时，他们能否经得起考验。总而言之，说了这么多数据来给朋友们说些干货，现在到底应该怎么操作？第一，我认为一定要做的就是我们的核心仓位，千万不要动。 但这个大前提是一定要，确保我们手中的股票是高质量，已经有稳定的现金流和健康的财务报表，并且估值也处在一个相对合理的水平的股票。 这一类股票才能作为核心仓位。那朋友们肯定会问，既然我们觉得大概率要跌，我先把它卖了，跌完再买回来不是更好吗？我们来算一笔账，如果我们想通过这个操作赚钱，需要连续做对两个决定，就是卖在跌之前，买在涨之前。那刚才我们说过，历史数据告诉我们，这种回撤是又深又短的。 底部很可能只有三五天。 所以绝大部分人实际的操作结果是卖掉之后市场先反弹，我们又不敢追了，等真跌下来了，觉得还会更低，还是不敢买，然后又错过了迅速的反弹，所以很可能在最后经历了一番的操作，又换来了一个更高的成本。总之，一个决定做对的概率已经不高了。两个连续做对，那是赌博，不是投资。 第二点就是对核心仓位以外的股票进行适当的减仓，但减仓要按规则减，不要按情绪减。我们从来不去试图预测顶部在哪里，我们要做的就是和朋友们强调过无数次的去系统性的兑现利润。 那这个方法也很简单，我们盯住一个关键的技术位，比如标普五百这一轮的最高点是8月13日的7799，如果接下来指数反复冲这个位置，两次三次都上不去，那就是一个明显的信号，我们就可以把那些涨的最多最拥挤的仓位去进行部分的止盈。 那注意我们要做的是部分的止盈，而不是清仓。这是为了让我们手中留有部分的现金，一旦出现机会时，我们还有钱能够补进去。但如果没有出现大幅度的下跌，我们也不会完全的踏空。 第三点就是我们把购物清单写出来，提前确定下来我们想要抄底的股票，并且写上明显的价位。那这一点现在听起来或许非常简单，因为我们心情是非常平静的，可以理性的判断哪些公司值得买买在什么位置。但当市场出现大规模回调的时候。 我们心态也会出现很大的变化，所以等到那个时候再去找公司买，肯定会变得更难一些。因此现在我们写一个清单，就是给未来那个惊慌的自己准备的，而且买的时候也不要一次性的完成建仓，可以分成两到三笔。这样做的目的并不是买在最低点，而是确保我们一定能够买到相对合适的价格。 同时避免因为恐慌完全错过了这样的机会。 第四点，我们要做的就是留现金，并且不要用过度的杠杆，无论是快速的涨还是跌，在一个我们已经明知道波动会放大的窗口里加杠杆是最没有必要的风险现金在这种时候。 不是闲置，它反而是一个期权。如果风险没有发生，我们本来就有仓位在市场里，但如果风险发生了，现金就是全场最值钱的东西。那现在市场的机会到底在哪里？ 我给朋友们分享一个筛选的角度，今天的AI板块已经彻底分化了，买AI这个说法本身已经失效了当一次利率驱动的抛售来临时，它是不分青红皂白的好公司，坏公司都会一起打折，但区别就是有些跌的幅度大，有些跌的幅度小，有些之后会迅速反弹，有些永远就跌下去了。我们举几个简单的例子。 做定制芯片设计的，它们的护城河是关系型的架构的知识产权在客户手里，供应商是执行方，这个活别人也能干，客户完全有动机去培养，第二家来压价。 所以对他来说，客户的集中度在市场下行中反而会成为一个巨大的风险。但是高带宽内存是不一样的，全球能做的就这么三家中国被出口管制挡在外面，光刻产是硬约束。 新建一座厂要四年和两百亿美元起步，就算是最大的客户，他也走不掉，所以同样都是客户集中一个是致命伤，而另一个完全不算风险，甚至完全不重要。 所以判断风险的标准不是他卖给谁，而是客户能不能走。因此，在这两种之间选择存储依然是最优项。那总而言之，九月份和中期选举，再加上美联储这三个因素。 都告诉我们，九月份很可能出现大盘层面的回调。但我们要做的并不是立即清仓，而是接下来这段时间我们做好心理准备，并且把现金准备好。 因为历史数据告诉我们，在历史上过去16次中期选举年中，恐慌型卖出都是错的，反而在低点附近敢于加仓，之后的一年中都拿到了非常不错的回报。 那当然我们不能够保证历史会再次重演，没有人能够打这个保票。今年的美联储的确比过去几年都要鹰派，这是真实的风险，但我们可以知道的就是，打折的永远是价格，不能打折的，是我们的纪律和选择，市场会给我们机会，问题只是那一天来的时候，我们是恐慌型抛售了，还是。
